title: Consolidation Module 2
description: The consolidation module that puts Module Three (entertainment and travel) and Module Four (science and technology) back on the table as nine tasks: rebuilding an argumentative paragraph from the marks its sentences carry — This, That and Such developing what came before, What is more and Furthermore adding to the same side, On the other hand turning to the other one, While and Although conceding before objecting, a pronoun waiting for the person named earlier — and the fault of putting a drawback behind a marker of addition; the vocabulary a hotel brochure lives on (leisure, relax, spend, sauna, magazine, beauty, book, and the spa bath, steam room, fitness room, hairdresser, award winning salon, comfy chairs and well-equipped club around them), with leisure as a stretch of time rather than a kind of amusement and to book as keeping a place in advance rather than demanding one; reading the situation of a text rather than its language — the type of text, where it would be read, and the three columns speaker, audience and occasion — with the marks that give a genre away and the rule that each dot of an unfinished word stands for one letter; the fifteen words of the module sorted into Entertainment and Science / Technology, and the beat they take when read aloud, with the ending -ing and the ending -ment leaving the stress where the base word had it, -tion and -sion pulling it onto the syllable in front of them, and a word spelt out letter by letter taking its beat on the last letter; the two opposed arguments about genetic engineering printed side by side and the question the book refuses to answer — the case for strict control with life evolving slowly, the genes as the building blocks of nature, scientists allowed to play God, and what a government might do with the perfect baby or a master-race, against the case for going on with genetic engineering used to help fight disease, a problem detected before it is passed on, genes altered and disease cured, plants that resist disease particularly in poor countries, animals bred to be more profitable, and the objection that progress is unnatural answered by the knowledge being used responsibly and by the precedent of transplant surgery; the language those two texts are written in — the three slots of a list of arguments (To begin with, furthermore, Lastly and In the first place, Secondly, Finally), the addition marker that can sit between two commas in the middle of its sentence, and For example which illustrates instead of adding; hedging with might and could against will and must; the fixed phrase in the wrong hands, letting a thing go on, and what has got out of hand; where an -ly adverb stands according to what it modifies, and the sentence adverb at the head that is the writer's own comment and not a description of the subject; a news item told in the simple past, the past perfect and the passive, with by used only if a name or a noun giving necessary information is included; seven sentence openings finished from their grammar against eight completions, after having plus a past participle read for who acted, and have something done split by the meaning of the verb between what was arranged and what simply happened; and a bare text given back its marks — the capital and the full stop, the comma splice English refuses, the comma of a list, the colon that opens a general term out into its members, the capitals of a film title and of the name of an award, and the trap of capitalising an important common noun.
